description.narrative: IFC is seeking to invest in a privately placed unsecured bond (the Bond) of up to US$90 million to be issued by Municipality of Ulaanbaatar (MUB), the subnational entity of the capital city of Mongolia. The investment entails (i) an own account IFC investment of up to US$65 million and (ii) an investment by IFC-Canada Blended Climate Finance Program (BCFP) of up to US$25 million. The proceeds of the financing will be used for the procurement by the MUB of the supply and construction for the 50MW/200MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project. The BESS is designed to store electricity during off-peak times and supply it during peak times (the Project), reducing recurrent blackouts during peak demand in the winters and provide grid stabilization.

The main Project outcomes are increasing the supply of reliable electricity in the Ulaanbaatar municipality and reducing electricity shortages which result in frequent blackouts. Beyond these effects, the investment can contribute to the resilience of the power sector by integrating energy storage solutions designed to smooth power production and mitigate interruptions during peak demand, as well as reduce the countrys need for expensive electricity imports. In the future, the expansion of BESS capacity in the MUBs central grid will prevent curtailment of renewable energy (RE) projects and facilitate the integration of RE capacity into Mongolias power mix.
